title: Budget Billing Missed-Installment Limits and Removal Terms by Plan
content:
# Budget Billing — Missed-Installment Limits and Removal Terms

Credit and Collections schedule for the six Budget Billing plans: the grace period after a bill's due date before an unpaid installment counts as missed, the number of missed installments that removes the customer from the plan, how the deferred balance is settled on removal, and how long a removal bars a new enrollment.

| Plan | Grace period after the due date | Missed installments within the plan that remove the customer | Settlement of the deferred balance on removal | Months after a removal before the customer may enroll again |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Residential Levelized Billing Plan | 5 calendar days | 2 | Deferred balance billed or credited on the next regular bill | 12 |
| Residential Budget Billing Plan | 5 calendar days | 2 | Deferred balance billed or credited on the next regular bill | 12 |
| Residential FlatBill Plan | 5 calendar days | 2 | Actual charges of the term to date less FlatBill amounts billed, billed or credited on the next regular bill | 12 |
| Commercial Levelized Billing Plan | 3 calendar days | 1 | Deferred balance billed or credited on the next regular bill | 12 |
| Commercial Budget Billing Plan | 3 calendar days | 1 | Deferred balance billed or credited on the next regular bill | 12 |
| Small Business FlatBill Plan | 3 calendar days | 1 | Actual charges of the term to date less FlatBill amounts billed, billed or credited on the next regular bill | 12 |

## Distinctions between the plans

- The three residential plans allow a grace period of 5 calendar days and remove the customer at the second missed installment; the three business plans allow 3 calendar days and remove the customer at the first.
- The four levelized and budget plans settle the deferred balance itself on removal. The two FlatBill plans settle the actual charges of the term to date less the FlatBill amounts billed in that term.
- The settlement is billed where it is owed by the customer and credited where it is in the customer's favour, on the next regular bill in every plan.
- The removal bar of 12 months is the same on every plan; it is counted on the customer's removals on any of the customer's service agreements.

## FlatBill removal settlement — hypothetical figures

On a Small Business FlatBill Plan removed in the fifth month of a term, actual charges for the term to date are $1,312.40 and FlatBill amounts billed in the term total $1,240.00. The settlement is $1,312.40 less $1,240.00, that is $72.40, billed on the next regular bill. Had actual charges been $1,190.00, the $50.00 shortfall below the FlatBill amounts billed would be credited on the next regular bill.
